gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-003 diagnoses the same characteristic-layer failure of the claimed near-second-order N-bound: an O(N^{-1}) contribution remains in the north/south layer estimates, so the asserted uniform bound cannot hold. It specifically identifies the mixed truncation term and its O(h)=O(N^{-1}) size, and explains that the barrier cannot absorb that residual. This fully recognizes the gold concern, although its presentation emphasizes the truncation-residual and barrier manifestation rather than explicitly reproducing the gold comparison-function B_3 decomposition.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: In the characteristic strips, the claimed second-order-in-N estimate is invalid because the discrete truncation/comparison argument leaves an O(N^{-1}) contribution: the mixed characteristic-layer term lacks the required decay, and the barrier cannot absorb the resulting residual. Thus only a first-order characteristic-layer rate is supported.
gold_decisions.uncovered_gold_detail: No substantive gold concern remains unrecognised. The prediction uses a different but mathematically equivalent broad manifestation of the unabsorbed O(N^{-1}) contribution rather than spelling out every B_3 comparison-function detail.

component_coverage.gold_component: The comparison function contains C N^{-1}B_3, with B_3=1 in the upper characteristic strip, producing an O(N^{-1}) contribution that cannot be absorbed into the claimed O(N^{-2}ln^2 N) bound.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction identifies an O(N^{-1}) residual in the characteristic-layer estimate, states that the proposed barrier cannot absorb it, and concludes that the claimed near-second-order bound must be weakened to first order. This recognizes the substantive unabsorbable O(N^{-1}) component even though it describes it through the residual/barrier formulation rather than naming B_3.

component_coverage.gold_component: The mixed characteristic-layer truncation term h_i min(1,h_i/epsilon) epsilon|w_{yyx}| is not reduced to second order because the stated derivative bounds provide no suitable east-boundary decay.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: The prediction quotes the same mixed truncation term, derives epsilon w_{N,xyy} from the layer equation, and shows it is generically O(1), making the coarse-mesh contribution O(N^{-1}) rather than second order.
